facts: The paper 'Social signals dominate clinician trust in medical AI' was authored by Aníbal Astobiza, Ramón Ortega Lozano, Marcos Alonso, and José Ríos-Díaz, published on arXiv on August 25, 2026 (id: arxiv:2611.00007).
The study introduces SPOT (Synergistic Process-Outcome Trust), a Bayesian framework modeling trust as inference over latent agent properties from outcome and process signals.
The researchers conducted a within-subjects vignette study with 275 Spanish healthcare professionals evaluating 16 clinical AI scenarios.
The scenarios tested three outcome signals (accuracy, intervention timing, prognosis) and five process signals (interface familiarity, explainability, team consensus, supervision, personalization).
Process signals accounted for 80.3 percent of the total absolute effect magnitude, whereas outcome signals accounted for only 19.7 percent.
Interface familiarity (beta = 0.71), team consensus (beta = 0.64), and explainability (beta = 0.63) showed strong effects (p < .001), while stated accuracy had a small effect (beta = 0.10).
Trust baselines were highly idiosyncratic and poorly predicted by participant demographics (R-squared = 0.06 under group-wise cross-validation).
The authors conclude that clinicians evaluate AI as social agents requiring social validation alongside technical verification.
